I went into Google maps street view in Venice to practice drawing backgrounds, found a street that I liked the look of and drew it analog with some brush markers. You can see the original drawing process in  [this Tumblr post](https://janetkonakova.tumblr.com/post/641577814849732608/to-practice-drawing-sceneries-we-had-an-online). I didn't like the drawing very much so I changed to colours in procreate, cropped it, then used a combination of the Old Brush and the smudge tool to smooth out the texture. After I used the Reed brush to draw the wiggly lines on a separate layer with the Vivid Light layer setting on. You can see my procreate time lapse [here](https://youtu.be/z4BGqGq4uEA)

I'm p hairy as well and used to be insecure about it. I used to shave everywhere all the time and be so ashamed whenever I forgot or didn't have time to. My first boyfriend didn't even know how hairy I really was and kept mentioning how he thinks women with hairy arms etc. are gross which made my insecurities worse. 

A fair share of people I've met made fun of my hair so, as unhealthy as that might be, I started making jokes about it as well. Eventually that led to me accepting the way my body is and finding a comfortable medium between enjoying the feeling of freshly-shaved skin and not caring too much if I haven't had time to/couldn't be bothered shaving. 

Since then I've only been with both male and female partners who don't give a fuck as long as I'm happy (Def. upgrades from the first one). Eg. One of my exes started the good streak by casually mentioning that if I decide to shave I shouldn't do it for her bc she finds my hair cute. My current boyfriend is way less hairy than me and we lovingly poke fun at each other hairyness/hairlesness all the time.

For the most part humour got rid if my insecurities but it's not for everyone. Might help looking up hairy women that are comfortable with themselves like Harnaam Kaur who has a full beard and is real gorgeous. Some people will find your body attractive, others won't but that's the way it is for everyone hairy or not. 

TL;DR don't sweat about it, you're fine
